title: Mature Cheddar Cheeseburger with Caramelised Onions
changes_from_base: Same patties and pan method as the Classic Cheeseburger. Onions are slowly caramelised first, thick mature cheddar is melted under a lid, and the sauce is a sharp Dijon mayo with rocket and pickles instead of ketchup, tomato and lettuce.
summary: A rich cheeseburger built around slow-caramelised onions, sharp melted cheddar and a mustard mayo for extra bite.
equipment: large heavy frying pan or cast-iron skillet (at least 26 cm)
lid or large upturned heatproof bowl

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
soft burger buns or brioche-style buns
Dijon mustard (choose one made without wine)

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Cook sliced onions in butter and oil with a pinch of salt over medium heat for 30-35 minutes, stirring every few minutes and adding a splash of water (1-2 tablespoons) whenever bits stick to the pan. They're ready when deep amber and jammy; tip them out and wipe the pan. Slow, steady browning develops deep, sweet, savoury flavour without scorching.

steps.title: Make the mustard mayo
steps.text: Mix mayo with Dijon mustard in a small bowl and set aside. A simple combination like this adds sharpness that cuts through the richness of the cheese and onions.

steps.title: Shape the patties
steps.text: Divide 600g cold beef mince into four 150g portions and shape into patties 11-12cm wide and about 1.5cm thick, pressing a shallow dimple into the centre of each. This keeps them flat rather than domed as they cook.

steps.title: Chill before cooking
steps.text: Chill the shaped patties for 10 minutes so the fat firms up. A cold patty holds its shape and sears more evenly in the hot pan.

steps.title: Season just before cooking
steps.text: Season both sides with salt and pepper only once ready to cook, since early salting makes the mince springy rather than tender. Toast the buttered buns cut-side down over medium heat for 1-2 minutes and set aside.

steps.title: Sear the first side
steps.text: Heat the pan over medium-high for 3 minutes, add 1 teaspoon of oil, then cook the patties (2 at a time, or all 4 in a 30cm pan) untouched for 4 minutes. A deep brown crust that releases easily is the sign to flip.

steps.title: Flip and melt the cheddar
steps.text: Flip once and cook for a further 3 minutes, adding thick slices of mature cheddar for the final 1.5 minutes under a lid. Mature cheddar is firmer and drier than processed cheese, so it needs that trapped heat to melt through properly. The patties are done at 71°C in the centre; rest for 2 minutes before building.

steps.title: Build the burger
steps.text: Spread the mustard mayo on both cut sides, then layer rocket, the cheddar-topped patty, a generous heap of caramelised onions and pickles. The peppery rocket balances the sweetness of the onions and the richness of the melted cheese.

tips: Don't rush the onions - 30-35 minutes of low, slow cooking is what turns them jammy and sweet rather than just softened.
Cover the pan to melt mature cheddar; it's firmer and drier than processed slices and needs the trapped heat to melt through.
Wipe the pan after the onions so the patties get a clean, dry sear rather than steaming in leftover liquid.
Season the patties only just before cooking to keep the mince tender.
storage: Cooked patties and caramelised onions keep separately in the fridge for up to 2 days; the patties also freeze well for up to 2 months without toppings. Reheat everything until piping hot and the patty reaches 74°C at the centre. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
